subject: Atlas Health renewal: commit increase + latency hotspots
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: planning for renewal – quick health snapshot

Hi Vivek,

We hit a much higher production footing in May after the new clinical ingestion pipeline went live. Token spend spiked ~3.5x month-over-month and we’re seeing a few latency outliers in us-west during peak windows. Contract is up in September and Carlos and I want to understand options for a bump to committed capacity + any short-term remediation you can recommend so we don’t incur unpredictable overage costs.

Numbers we have so far (May -> June):
- Avg daily tokens: 27M -> 95M
- P95 latency (us-west): 380ms -> 620ms on model: redwood-open-vicuna-13b
- Error retries: 0.6% -> 1.7%

Can we get a short call and a concise proposal (capacity options + any immediate config changes) this week?

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product
Atlas Health
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: planning for renewal – quick health snapshot

Elena — thanks for the note and the figures, that spike explains the sudden cost volatility. I can run a short ops review and put together 2–3 concrete paths:

1) Short-term: temporary burst credit + routing tweak (shift a portion of inference to us-east during peak) to reduce us-west latency outliers.
2) Mid-term: commit increase (annual) to lock in unit economics and pool-optimized routing.
3) Long-term: model variant / quantization recommendation for the highest-volume endpoints.

Quick asks before the call so I can come prepared:
- Can you share a CSV export of token breakdown by endpoint (hourly if possible)?
- Are there any strict latency SLOs for particular endpoints (eg. triage vs document summarization)?

I’m available Thu 22nd 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 23rd 13:00–14:00 PT for a 30-min call. Which works?

—Vivek
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: planning for renewal – quick health snapshot

Folks — great meeting yesterday. Summary and recommended options below (attached: usage_report_q2.csv, proposed_terms_ATLAS_v1.pdf):

Summary of findings
- April baseline: ~27M daily tokens; June steady-state: ~85–95M daily tokens with concentrated spikes 12:00–14:00 PT.
- Hotspot: us-west instances show 60–80ms tail regressions tied to longer sequences on the triage endpoint.
- Opportunity: 14% token-cost improvement with model variant + prefix caching on the triage flow.

Recommended commercial paths (two options)
A) Annual Commit + Headroom Guard (preferred)
- Commit: 30B tokens/year (2.5x current annualized run-rate)
- Discount: 18% off list token price
- Headroom Guard: auto-burn up to +30% monthly; excess abates into credits if average monthly usage over trailing 3 months drops below commit by >20% (downside protection language included in attached PDF)
- Operational: staged rollout: week 0–2 canary to us-east routing + KV prefix caching; week 3–4 scale commit pool and shift 60% of bulk traffic to optimized kernels.

B) Quarterly Flex + Burst Credits (short-term)
- Quarter commit: 8B tokens/quarter; includes 60% discounted burst credits for sudden spikes.
- No long-term pricing guarantee.

Technical mitigations (quick wins)
- Enable prefix/KV caching for triage endpoint (immediate) — estimated 10–14% token savings.
- Route 25–40% of inference to us-east during 12:00–14:00 PT window (can be automated via routing policy).
- Apply quantization suggestion on non-critical summarization models (approx. 6–8% cost reduction).

Next steps
- Please review the attached proposed_terms_ATLAS_v1.pdf and usage_report_q2.csv.
- If you prefer path A, Ben will craft legal/reg terms and I’ll coordinate a migration runbook.
- If path B, we can authorize burst credits immediately and follow up on a quarterly commit cadence.

Attachments: usage_report_q2.csv (attachment stub), proposed_terms_ATLAS_v1.pdf (attachment stub)

—Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@atlashealth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: planning for renewal – quick health snapshot

Thanks Vivek — review complete. Atlas leadership prefers Option A (Annual Commit + Headroom Guard). A few quick asks before we route to procurement/legal:

1) Please attach the SOC2 summary and the exact fallback SLA for cross-region routing (we need assurance on failback timelines).
2) Confirm the credit abatement calculation example in section 3.2 of the PDF (Carlos will validate internally).
3) Can we get a 30-day revocation window in case an acquisition or product pivot causes consumption to materially change?

If you can add the items above and send an updated PDF, procurement will aim to route for signature week of July 24. Attaching our internal usage export for reference (usage_export_from_atlas.csv).

Appreciate the clear options — happy to proceed once we have the SOC2 and the small term edits.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director of Product
Atlas Health
